newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Andean Pact-Mercosur agreement seen for late 1997.
newsitem.headline: Andean Pact-Mercosur agreement seen for late 1997.

text.p: Venezuelan and Uruguayan leaders signed a series of agreements Tuesday and said they were committed to seeing an agreement between South America's two main trading blocs by the end of the year.

Venezuela's President Rafael Caldera and Uruguay's President Julio Maria Sanguinetti signed a joint statement that said there was a "high possibility" of an accord between the Andean Community and Mercosur in the second half of 1997.
"The countries of the Southern Cone Common Market (Mercosur) support progressive commercial liberalization in the hemisphere," said Sanguinetti, who is on a three-day official visit to Venezuela.

Venezuela and its Andean Community partners -- Colombia, Bolivia and Ecuador -- are due to meet Mercosur representatives in Brazil in December to set out a structure to link up with the trade bloc that groups Brazil, Argentina, Paraguay and Uruguay.
Caldera and Sanguinetti also signed an investment protection and promotion agreement; an extradition treaty and accords on judicial, educational and social security cooperation.
Trade between the two countries reached $43 million in 1996 and both presidents said they would study ways to improve cooperation in the energy sector.
Sanguinetti's three day visit ends Wednesday.
